title: IT Support Security Alert

transcript.speaker: Caller
transcript.text: Hi, this is Marcus from IT Support. How are you today?

transcript.speaker: You
transcript.text: I'm good, thanks. What can I help you with?

transcript.speaker: Caller
transcript.text: We're doing routine security updates on all company accounts. I need to verify your employee ID for our records.

transcript.speaker: You
transcript.text: Sure, it's on my badge. Let me check the HR portal first.

transcript.speaker: Caller
transcript.text: No problem. You can also submit a ticket through the IT portal if you prefer, and we'll follow up via email.

transcript.speaker: Caller
transcript.text: URGENT! This is IT Security. Your account has been compromised!

transcript.speaker: Caller
transcript.text: We detected suspicious login attempts. I need your password immediately to secure your account before it's locked!

transcript.speaker: You
transcript.text: My password? Are you sure that's the right procedure?

transcript.speaker: Caller
transcript.text: Yes! We don't have time. Also, what's the code from your authenticator app? We need it NOW!

explainTitle: Correct! You spotted the vishing attempt.
explainPoints: Aggressive urgency and panic: The scammer uses 'URGENT!' and 'NOW!' to pressure you into acting without thinking. Legitimate IT staff remain calm and professional.
Requesting passwords directly: Real IT departments NEVER ask for your password, PIN, or MFA codes over the phone. They can reset accounts without this information.
Suspicious phone number: The number +1 (844) 729-8844 is an external toll-free number, not an internal extension. Always verify by calling the official IT helpdesk number.
No verification offered: Legitimate IT staff will provide their employee ID, offer to send confirmation emails, or suggest you call back through official channels.
